rule: For each grid corner, take the one-colour 4-connected object containing the corner cell (none if the cell is background). Translate it one corner clockwise (TL->TR->BR->BL->TL) so its bounding box sits flush in the destination corner. Paint only its cells over the input, reading every source from the original input. Uncovered old cells survive, and empty corners send nothing.
scope: Copy each original corner-connected monochrome component one corner clockwise by translation, preserving existing pixels outside its stamped cells and reading every source from the original input.
constraints: Four canonical pairs and1000 independent seeds pass exactly; all1000 random inputs distinct.

stress_test.limitations: Bounded randomized agreement with a saved solver is not proof of semantic completeness.

authored_scope: Supported: background 7 by default, with any other background accepted. Sides are sampled mostly from 7..16, the fixture range. Sides 17..30 and non-square grids are synthetic extensions, and explicit random sides of 5..30 are accepted. Corner objects are random rectangles or 4-connected blobs. By default 2-4 corners are occupied; num_corners requests exactly 1..4. Distractors include near-miss objects beside empty corners. They may touch different-colour corner objects, and may touch each other (different colours, or same colour diagonally only). Corner objects may share colours. Explicit corners/others reconstruct the fixtures. Not supported in random mode: distractors orthogonally or diagonally touching a same-colour corner object; corner objects of half the grid size or more; overlapping clockwise stamps.
authored_constraints: Each declared corner object equals the one-colour 4-connected input component at its corner cell.
Declared empty corners are background; distractors never cover corner cells.
No distractor is 8-adjacent to a same-colour corner object, so 4- and 8-connected readings of corner objects agree in random scenes.
Same-colour distractors are never orthogonally adjacent.
Corner objects are smaller than half the grid in each dimension, so stamps never overlap and corner objects never touch.
Background is strictly the most frequent input colour.
At least one corner is occupied and output != input (enforced in both explicit and random modes).
Integer controls reject bools and non-integers.
